name: QGIS 3
negative_boundary: Ultra-heavy raw LiDAR point clouds > 50M pts
article_note: Only open source GIS that can compete with ArcGIS Pro (35 differences documented). QGIS plugins give you the power to analyze like the Incredible Hulk.

name: GRASS GIS
negative_boundary: High-end cartographic production or dynamic web map styling
article_note: Developed by US Army Corps of Engineers. Trusted by NASA, NOAA, USDA, and USGS. Over 350 rock-solid vector and raster manipulation tools.

name: Whitebox GAT
negative_boundary: Interactive vector digitization and publication-grade cartography
article_note: Replaced Terrain Analysis System (TAS) for hydro-geomorphic applications. The Swiss-army knife of LiDAR data with 410+ tools.

name: Birdi
negative_boundary: Traditional GIS desktop spatial analysis, complex vector topological editing
article_note: Not completely free per se, offers generous free tier. Perfect for drone inspection, infrastructure asset assessment and severity tracking.

name: gvSIG
negative_boundary: Extensive English API documentation and non-Java mobile OS ecosystem
article_note: After QGIS, next best option. Impressive OpenCAD tools, agile NavTable for vertical record inspection, and gvSIG Mobile for field GPS work.

name: ILWIS
negative_boundary: Complex multi-layer vector digitizing and modern drag-and-drop layer workflows
article_note: Once commercial, now open source. Integrated Land and Water Information Management. Extinction-proof tool for planners, biologists, and water managers.

name: SAGA GIS
negative_boundary: Print cartography layout and vector symbology design
article_note: System for Automated Geoscientific Analyses. Prime choice for DEMs: Topographic Wetness Index, morphometry, and closing raster data gaps.

name: GeoDa
negative_boundary: Raster DEM processing, LiDAR manipulation, and field GPS capture
article_note: Gateway to spatial data exploration and spatial statistics. Embraced by Harvard, MIT, and Cornell for health, real estate, and economic modeling.

name: MapWindow 5
negative_boundary: Non-Windows OS environments and native Python-first automation
article_note: Originated from US EPA 'Basins' contract. Bundles TauDEM for automatic watershed delineation, HydroDesktop, and DotSpatial architecture.

name: uDig
negative_boundary: Complex spatial analysis, heavy raster modeling, stability on large datasets
article_note: User-friendly Desktop Internet GIS. Consumes OGC web standards (WMS, WFS, WPS) and runs cleanly on Mac, Windows, Linux with Mapnik integration.

name: OpenJUMP
negative_boundary: Advanced remote sensing imagery pipelines and 3D elevation rendering
article_note: JAVA Unified Mapping Platform. Outstanding vector conflation project that grew into a robust package handling large vector datasets.

name: FalconView
negative_boundary: Civilian research, commercial land use planning, non-tactical spatial analysis
article_note: Built by Georgia Tech for DoD and National Geospatial-Intelligence Agencies for combat flight planning. DEFENSE RESTRICTED DOMAIN.

name: OrbisGIS
negative_boundary: Mission-critical production pipelines, unassisted non-research users
article_note: Cross-platform GIS designed by and for research. Executes noise maps and hydrology without add-ons, but documentation is still maturing.

name: Diva GIS
negative_boundary: General-purpose enterprise GIS, high-volume vector editing, modern cloud workflows
article_note: Specializes in mapping biological richness and species diversity distribution including DNA marker data and WorldClim climate extractions.
